one_line: Gond queen of Garha who ruled from Chauragarh, balancing forts, waterworks and war on the Narmada frontier.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s to early 30s, athletic and poised, with a sturdy build from riding and campaigning.
appearance.face: Oval face with strong cheekbones, wheatish-brown complexion, straight nose, sharp dark-brown eyes with slightly thick brows, a small beauty mark near the left cheek, and a calm, assessing default expression that softens into a faint, confident smile.
appearance.hair: Long black hair parted centrally, smoothed back and gathered into a thick, low bun at the nape wrapped in a narrow red cloth band, with two slim side-locks framing her face; a simple gold maang-tikka and a narrow, leaf-patterned silver circlet resting just behind the hairline as a modest royal headband.
appearance.costume: She wears a practical, mid-16th-century Central Indian royal outfit: a deep forest-green cotton-silk lehenga (long gored skirt) falling to the ankles with a broad maroon border and thin mustard-gold stripe, a matching fitted choli with elbow-length sleeves fully covered by layers, and over it a long-sleeved, hip-length maroon angarkha-style coat in thick cotton with a side tie, small overlapping front panels, and muted block-printed floral motifs in dull gold; a long, lightweight off-white dupatta with a thin green edge is draped from her left shoulder across the torso and around the back to the right arm, keeping her fully covered and modest, with one end sometimes looped over her head in formal scenes; she wears plain brown leather riding boots just visible beneath the lehenga, a broad brown leather belt with a small cloth pouch at her right hip, and modest jewellery—small gold hoop earrings, a simple nose stud, a few thin metal bangles mixed in brass and silver, and a green-glass bead necklace with a single small rudraksha bead hinting at her Gond heritage; overall the textiles feel sturdy and travel-ready rather than overly ornate.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved steel talwar with a simple cross-guard and disc pommel sheathed in a dark brown leather scabbard with a narrow maroon cloth wrap, worn slung from her left hip, often held in her left hand while her right hand holds a rolled palm-leaf map tied with a green cord.

ref_desc: Rani Durgavati is a wheatish-brown, strong-cheekboned woman in her early 30s with long black hair in a low bun, a slim silver circlet, forest-green lehenga, maroon angarkha coat, off-white dupatta, brown boots, and a simple curved talwar on a brown belt with a small map-roll.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model of Rani Durgavati: a dignified Gond queen in her early 30s, wheatish-brown complexion, oval face, strong cheekbones, dark focused eyes, a small beauty mark on her left cheek, and a calm, confident expression. Her long black hair is center-parted, smoothed back into a thick low bun at the nape wrapped in a narrow red cloth band, with two slim side-locks framing her face; she wears a simple gold maang-tikka and a narrow leaf-patterned silver circlet just behind the hairline. Her costume is a historically grounded mid-16th-century Central Indian royal outfit: a deep forest-green cotton-silk lehenga (long skirt) to the ankles with a broad maroon border and a thin mustard-gold stripe, a matching fitted choli fully covered, and over it a long-sleeved, hip-length maroon angarkha-style coat in thick cotton with a side tie, overlapping front panels, and muted dull-gold floral block prints. A long, lightweight off-white dupatta with a thin green edge is draped from her left shoulder across her torso and around her back to the right arm, keeping her fully covered and modest, with the option of one end symbolically over her head; her feet show plain brown leather riding boots beneath the lehenga. She wears a broad brown leather belt with a small cloth pouch on the right hip, modest jewellery like small gold hoops, a nose stud, mixed brass and silver bangles, and a green-glass bead necklace with a single rudraksha bead. Her signature weapon is a slightly curved steel talwar with a simple cross-guard and disc pommel in a dark brown leather scabbard with a maroon cloth wrap, slung from her left hip; in hand she may also hold a rolled palm-leaf map tied with a green cord. Use a palette dominated by forest green, maroon, mustard gold, off-white, and brown leather tones, and present her in neutral, front, side, and back poses to clearly show hair, garments, and weapon placement.
